This appeal under Section Aaytu Ram Kashyap vs Rishab Dev Tiwari on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146168729/
1 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short "MV Act") has been filed challenging the award dated Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:1748 09.02.2018 passed in Claim Case No. 102/2017 by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bastar at Jagdalpur, district Bastar (CG).
2.

sentences.text:
By the impugned award, the learned Tribunal has awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.
2,30,000/- in favour of the appellants/ claimants on account of death of deceased Rohit Kashyap aged about 14 years in an accident that took place on 25.10.2016 by rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle truck bearing registration No. CG04 HN3197 driven by respondent No.1/driver owned by respondent No.2/owner and insured with the Insurance Company.

The claim application under Section 166 of the Act of 1988 was filed claiming total compensation of Rs. 13,50,000/-
against the respondents inter alia
pleading that the deceased was aged about 14 years and he was a student, he would have definitely been successful in his life and would have contributed in the livelihood of the appellants.

3. The claim application was resisted by the respondents on various grounds including the insurance company taking a plea that the offending vehicle was driven in violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
The learned Tribunal having framed issues, decided the same in favour of the appellants/claimants and awarded the aforesaid compensation.

4. Shri Pankaj Singh, learned counsel for the appellants/claimants submits that though the deceased was aged about 14 years and was an intelligent child, having a bright future ahead and would have assisted the family in future by his income, the compensation cannot be equated in terms of money.

He placed his reliance upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Kurvan Ansari Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:1748 @ Kurvan Ali and Another Vs. Shyam Kishore Murmu and Another (2022)1 SCC 317 and Kishan Gopal and Another Vs. Lala and Others (2014) 1SCC 244 and contends that at least Rs. 5,00,000/- ought to have been awarded.
5.

entities.text: Kurvan Ansari Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:1748 @ Kurvan Ali and Another Vs. Shyam Kishore Murmu and Another (2022)1 SCC 317
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Kishan Gopal and Another Vs. Lala and Others (2014) 1SCC 244
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent No.3/Insurance Company supports the impugned award and submits that just compensation has been awarded as the deceased was not an earning person.

6. Taking the entire facts and circumstances of the case and in the light of the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Kurvan Ansari (supra) and Kishan Gopal (supra), this Court feel inclined to allow Rs. 5,00,000/- as compensation to the appellants and it is so awarded.

After deducting Rs. 2,30,000/- as awarded by the learned Tribunal enhanced amount comes to Rs.
2,70,000/-.
Respondent No.3/Insurance Company shall pay the amount of Rs. 2,70,000/- within a period of 60 days with 6% interest from the date of claim application.
After deposit, the learned Tribunal shall pass appropriate order with regard to apportionment, investment and disbursement of enhanced compensation.
7. With this observation, the appeal is thus partly allowed.
